back: Used in formal regulations and warnings (e.g., 'Bookings must be made') [11].
Used to remind ourselves to do something [11].
Use 'must have + past participle' (e.g., 'She must have borrowed it') [11].
Use 'must be + -ing' (e.g., 'You must be imagining things') [11].
Use 'must be going to' or 'must be + -ing' [11].
Use 'has got to be' (e.g., 'He has got to be at least two metres tall!') [11].
Use 'must have to' or 'must have had to' (e.g., 'You must have to put in a password') [11].
Prefer 'have (got) to' in questions for hope/negative answer expect [11].
Use 'have to' (not must) with adverbs like 'often, always, never' [11].
Use 'had to' especially in questions and negative sentences [11].
Do NOT use 'have got to' with other modals (e.g., 'Motorists will have to wait') [11].
